functions.name: send
functions.description: Send a message as a configured account. With no `account` and `channel` it answers the chat of your latest pushed line, in its thread. A seat names another of its chats by its label, such as `DM` or `#general`. `file` uploads a file from your own node (an absolute path, up to 24 MiB), such as a plan's .md, with `text` as its message; `text` is optional with a file. `files` attaches several: each an absolute path on your node, or an inline {filename, text}. Discord takes files up to 10 MB, and the Opal Slack bot up to the 24 MiB a call carries. A DM where nobody but the bot has written is refused. `quiet` keeps the replies in the sent message's thread from its chat's seat holder.

functions.name: react
functions.description: Put an emoji reaction on a message, or take it off with `remove`. With no ids it reacts to your latest pushed line. `emoji` is a character, a name or :name:. Discord and the Opal Slack bot react.

functions.name: fetch
functions.description: Fetch a channel's existing messages live from the platform (incl. ones from before the service started), with attachment metadata. `before` pages backwards. Nothing is stored — the platform is the source of truth.

functions.name: history
functions.description: Read a bot account's synced history of every chat the bot is in (edits applied, deletes hidden unless `include_deleted`). Newest `limit` messages, or with `since` (a message ts) the ones after it, oldest first — the catch-up read after `awm services listen social message`. Also lists each chat's sync cursor.

functions.name: seats
functions.description: List the chats a bot account is in, each with the session holding it or null. A chat that [seats] in social.toml declares a seat also shows its seat: the state (empty, starting, occupied), its agent's session id and node, its level and its queued lines. Social starts a seat's agent on the seat's first new message. The seat stops its agent after 4 hours with no message and no running turn, and the next message resumes the same conversation.

functions.name: mount
functions.description: Hold a seat: every new message in that chat, from anyone but the bot, is typed into your prompt as one line '[<server>/<chat>/<sender>, <level>] ↳<thread> <text>'. Background sessions only. One holder per seat: a held seat is refused unless `force`, which takes it and tells the old holder. A session below trusted never holds a trusted chat. A Discord DM is a seat only for an operator. A declared seat is refused: its host's `seats adopt` hands it a session. The result's `rename` gives the seat's session name, seat:<app>/<server>/<chat>.

params.name: channel
params.description: A seat's id or name, as `seats` lists it.

functions.name: unmount
functions.description: Release a seat you hold, or every seat you hold on the account when `channel` is omitted.

functions.name: forward
functions.description: Forward a message from a chat you hold to another seat. Its agent gets the line, and may read your chat's history for 24 hours. An empty seat starts its agent, except a DM nobody has opened. With no `message_id` it forwards your latest pushed line.

params.name: channel
params.description: The seat to forward to: its id or name, as `seats` lists it.

params.name: account
params.description: The target seat's account. Default: the source chat's.

params.name: note
params.description: One line for the receiving agent.

functions.name: seat_remote_control
functions.description: Set a seat's Remote Control switch, which every agent the seat starts follows. The seat's host applies it to the live session on its next pull, so `live` answers `pending`. Only operations on this node calls it, for the Remote Control switch on Ops.

functions.name: seat_refresh
functions.description: Pick a seat's model and effort, which win over social.toml. The seat's host restarts an agent it started on them once the agent is between turns, resuming its conversation, and keeps them for the next start of an empty seat. `live` answers `pending`. Only operations on this node calls it, for the Refresh button on Ops.

functions.name: seat_pull
functions.description: A seat host's seats plugin holds this to take the rows waiting for its node. `ack_through` acks every row through that id. Not for sessions.

functions.name: seat_report
functions.description: A seat host's seats plugin sends one row of its outbox. A row already applied is answered and not applied again. Not for sessions.

functions.name: seat_act
functions.description: A seat host's seats plugin reacts to a message (`action` react) or downloads its attachments (`action` download) in a chat its node answers. Not for sessions.

functions.name: download_attachments
functions.description: Download a message's attachments to a fresh temp dir on the node you call from (outside the awm workspace). Re-fetches the message live; returns `dir` and each file's `path`, `filename`, `mime`, `size`. Files together may not pass 24 MiB. `idx` optionally selects a single attachment.

functions.name: accounts
functions.description: List configured accounts with platform, kind, and live status.

functions.name: channels
functions.description: List channels visible to a configured account. `include_dms=true` also enumerates direct/group DMs (kind 'dm'/'group') where the platform supports it.

functions.name: open_dm
functions.description: Resolve a platform user (by id, or by name where the platform supports it) to a direct-message channel and open it. Returns the channel for use with fetch/send.

functions.name: list_operators
functions.description: List whitelisted operators, optionally by platform.

functions.name: add_operator
functions.description: Whitelist a platform user and map them to an awm_user.

functions.name: remove_operator
functions.description: Remove a platform user from the whitelist.

functions.name: lookup
functions.description: Resolve a (platform, user id) to its awm_user (or null).

functions.name: emit_probe
functions.description: Emit a synthetic, inert `command` event carrying only `nonce`, so a subscriber can prove on demand that it can still receive. Opens no window, arms nothing, sends no message.
